findings.location: row gso::opt1-102, fields version_status and version (criterion c2 lifecycle; also c1 registry version)
findings.evidence: Row claims version_status "published" with version "opt1-102". c2 defines "published" as: the maintainer publishes a release identifier for this board and the version copies it. Neither Source 1 (protocol page text, including the full changelog dated 2025-11-03 through 2026-09-27) nor Source 2 (leaderboard.json; metadata only "last_updated":"2026-09-27" and "total_tasks":102) publishes any release identifier for this board; "opt1-102" copies no maintainer identifier, and changelog dates plus last_updated are timestamps, not board release identifiers. Per c2, a page publishing no release identifier supports only "snapshot"; "published" here is a mismatch. All other c1/c2 fields verified: metric text matches the page's Opt@1 definition (>=95% human speedup, passes correctness tests); unit "percent" and range [0,100] agree with Source 4's served scale (32 values, min 0, max 88.24, consistent with Source 2's 32 Opt@1 rows out of 34); description matches page wording and 102 tasks/10 codebases/5 languages; version_guard conditions hold (total_tasks 102, settings in {Opt@1, Opt@10}, rows carry name/scaffold/setting/date); status "active" supported by Source 3 (4 added rows, nonzero => active per c2) and last_updated 2026-09-27; superseded_by null uncontradicted (page names no successor).
findings.repair: Change version_status to "snapshot" and version to a dated identity of the form snapshot-<date> per the registry convention, or, if a maintainer-published release identifier for this board exists, cite it in evidence and copy it into version.

uncertainties: Source 1 is a bounded excerpt of the page; the supplied text covers all visible sections (header, leaderboard, changelog, curves, compute profile, footer), but if an unexcerpted region published a release identifier, the version_status judgement should be rechecked.

I cannot recompute the owner row hash or recompute the generated summaries in Sources 3-4; I only sanity-checked them against Source 2 (34 model rows, 32 with Opt@1, lowest served score 0, highest 88.24) and found them internally consistent.
The maintainer label "GSO team (UC Berkeley)" is not stated verbatim in the Source 1 excerpt; it matches this run's own generated summaries in Sources 3-4, and the scope of c1/c2 does not require it.

Source 2 lists two Opt@10 rows (Claude Sonnet 3.5 V2, O4 Mini); Source 4's count of 32 implies the scale summary was read over Opt@1 values only, which is consistent with this identity but not explicitly stated in the summary text.
